description.narrative:
The Global Concessional Financing Facility (GCFF) is a fund that provides support to middle-income countries hosting large numbers of refugees, enabling them to access concessional loans under terms that are broadly comparable to those available to the poorest countries through IDA. The projects support the integration of refugees as well as assistance to host communities. The fund was originally established to support Jordan and Lebanon in their response to refugees from Syria. The World Bank administers the fund as a Financing Intermediary Facility (FIF). Countries borrow money for projects implemented by the World Bank/IBRD or by one of the regional development banks: ADB, IDB, IsDB, EBRD, and EIB.
The GCFF is now a global mechanism that covers several middle-income countries receiving large refugee inflows, among them Colombia and Ecuador, which host large numbers of refugees from Venezuela; Costa Rica from Nicaragua; Moldova from Ukraine; and Armenia from Azerbaijan. These countries are represented in the fund’s governing board together with the donors. The United Nations participates as an observer.
